beats.text: A figure in Victorian dress. That's what some people say they've seen at the Dole Mansion, in Crystal Lake, Illinois.
beats.label: CRYSTAL LAKE, ILLINOIS
beats.credit: What people report: Patch (2012); Northwest Herald (2023)

beats.text: It was built in 1865 for Charles Dole, a Chicago grain merchant. Later, ice was cut from the lake here.
beats.credit: History: Landmarks Illinois; The Dole; Crystal Lake Historical Society

beats.text: In 1922, a group that included Lou Ringling, widow of circus co-founder Al Ringling, turned it into a country club.
beats.label: THE COUNTRY CLUB
beats.credit: Landmarks Illinois; The Dole; Northwest Quarterly

beats.text: Later, Franciscans ran a boys' school here. In 2002, the community raised the money to save it from a condo developer.
beats.label: SAVED
beats.credit: Landmarks Illinois; The Dole; Northwest Quarterly

beats.text: Some believe Lou Ringling never left. A staff member has described drastic temperature changes. And visitors tell of a figure in Victorian dress.
beats.label: WHAT PEOPLE REPORT

beats.text: Not everyone believes it. But the stories keep coming.
beats.label: THE LEGEND

beats.text: Today the Dole is an arts center, open to the public.
beats.label: TODAY

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.

end_card.pill: The Dole, Crystal Lake: open to the public

factcheck.result: Ice harvest moved to 'later' (it was the son-in-law's era); 'grain baron' not 'ice baron'; Lou Ringling 'a group that included', Al a co-founder; 'a condo developer'; temperature changes from one staff member; 'figure' (sources say woman and girl); mansion redrawn at three storeys with a tower (exact tower shape and gables not verified); all narration supported
